outcome: Incidence of magnesium toxicity (loss of knee jerk)
cohort: The study included 120 patients diagnosed with eclampsia.
finding: The intravenous magnesium sulfate regimen was significantly more efficacious in controlling convulsions compared to the intramuscular regimen, maintaining higher and steadier serum magnesium levels, although it was associated with a slightly higher incidence of magnesium toxicity.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the prevalent mode of delivery (caesarean section) between the intravenous and intramuscular magnesium sulfate groups.
